Accommodation open for bookings before 1 April 2027 must be registered with the Welsh Revenue Authority (WRA) by 31 March 2027. Registration is free and mandatory across Wales, even where the local council has no visitor levy.

The WRA registration service opened on 1 October 2026. At launch it accepts new registrations only; updates to existing registrations were to open in early 2027, with changes to be updated by 31 March 2027.

You must register if all apply: you take bookings for overnight stays in visitor accommodation in Wales; you are responsible for the accommodation (own, rent, or act for the owner); and your bookings are for 31 nights or less. Covers self-catering lets, main homes/spare rooms, hotels, B&Bs, guesthouses, tent/caravan/motorhome pitches, glamping, static caravans, hostels and bunkhouses.

The register is run by the Welsh Revenue Authority under the Visitor Accommodation (Register and Levy) Etc. (Wales) Act 2025 (Royal Assent 18 September 2025). After registering you receive a unique registration number; some details appear on a public register.

Accommodation first offered for bookings on or after 1 April 2027 must be registered before it opens for bookings. Updates to registration details and deregistration must be made within 30 days of the change.

The penalty for failing to register, update, or deregister on time is £100 per premises (each address offered as accommodation counts as one premises). Penalties are payable within 30 days. Known conclusion (£100 late fine) confirmed against the official GOV.WALES penalties page.

area_or_topic: Escalating penalties for continued failure to register
key_point: If you still do not register, update or deregister after the first penalty, a further £10 per premises per day applies for up to 30 days; failing to register within those 30 days brings a further £1,000 penalty per premises. Maximum per premises: £1,400 (£100 + £300 + £1,000). The WRA may also register you itself; that counts as a late registration with the same penalties.

Rates are set Wales-wide by the Welsh Government: 75p per person per night for adults in shared rooms in hostels, bunkhouses, bothies or dormitories and for tent pitches; £1.30 per person per night for all other accommodation (including self-catering lets, hotels and B&Bs).
